# Verdin AM62P (Dahlia, Riverdi RVT70 1024x600 behind the SN65DSI83): the
# display path's registers read through /dev/mem while the board's Linux
# drove the panel (the boot splash / console; LVDS-1 connected and enabled,
# mode 1024x600). Test data for driver/rust/src/soc/am62p/display_golden.rs;
# the read list and why each address is safe to read:
# driver/docs/am62p-display-cold.md, board plan (a).
#
# Taken 2026-10-01T20:04Z (UTC; 2026-10-02 JST) on
#   Linux verdin-am62p-00000000 6.6.138-7.6.1 #1-Torizon SMP PREEMPT Fri May  8 07:27:41 UTC 2026 aarch64
# /proc/config.gz: CONFIG_STRICT_DEVMEM=y, CONFIG_IO_STRICT_DEVMEM not set,
# so the MMIO the drivers claim is readable as root: every address below was
# read (nothing blocked). Reads: one 32-bit load each (python3 mmap of
# /dev/mem + ctypes c_uint32), no writes; the FIFO-popping and write-only
# DSI registers (0x080, 0x08C, 0x090, 0x094, 0x0A0, 0x150..0x168) skipped.
# Linux's iomem: 301c0000-301c0fff phy, 30220000.dss common/vidl1/vid/ovr1/
# ovr2/vp1/vp2, 30270000-302700ff + 30500000-305fffff dsi.
# Linux's clocks (clk_summary): DSS fck 232:8 320 MHz, VP2 232:4 51.302 MHz,
# dsi_sys_clk 231:5 250 MHz, D-PHY pll_ref 238:1 25 MHz, psm 238:16 16 MHz.
#
# The WIZ question: 0x301c0000..0x14 read 0; MOD_VER 0x6992xxxx (MODULE_ID
# 992h) reads at 0x301c0f00. The WIZ is at +0xF00 as TI's driver has it, not
# at 0h as the SPRUJ83D register summary (14.8.6.3.2) says.
#
# SN65DSI83 on i2c-2 0x2c (i2cdump -f -y -r 0x00-0xef 2 0x2c b), not used
# by the test, kept for the bridge's record:
#   00: 35 38 49 53 44 20 20 20 01 00 83 10 00 01 00 00
#   10: 26 00 1e 00 00 00 00 00 78 05 03 00 00 00 00 00
#   20: 00 04 00 00 58 02 00 00 21 00 00 00 05 00 00 00
#   30: 0a 00 00 00 a0 00 17 00 a0 00 0c 00 00 00 00 00
#   40..ef: 00 (IRQ_EN E0 0, IRQ_STAT E5 0)
#
# Format: ADDRESS WIDTH VALUE (hex, 32, hex), in the order of the read list.
